svg.font-family: ui-sans-serif, system-ui, -apple-system, Segoe UI, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
svg.title: MedLattice: locking a patient record rather than hiding it
svg.desc: A five-panel diagram. Panel one: the conventional record is one container guarded by a permissions rule, so a misconfiguration, an injection flaw or a stolen database exposes everything, and ciphertext copied today can be decrypted once quantum computers arrive. Panel two: MedLattice splits the record into about twenty separately locked drawers and then into individually sealed envelopes, with a key tree from which a reader can derive only the keys beneath the one they were given. Panel three: what a receptionist, nurse, consultant, pharmacist, patient and IT department each receive, most tiles locked. Panel four: a shared append-only logbook held by hospital, laboratory and regulator, containing no medical data. Panel five: the break-glass emergency override, easy to use and impossible to hide. A footer lists the cryptography: ML-KEM-1024 with X448, ML-DSA-87 with Ed448, AES-256-GCM, and hash-only notarisation.
svg.text: — locking a patient record, not hiding it
One container. One login. A permissions table decides
what gets drawn on the screen.
Cannot see → can see. Instantly, completely.
Three in the morning, patient unconscious, no time
for any of this. So: easy to use, impossible to hide.
No approval to wait for, nobody to telephone.
Typed by the clinician, kept, reviewable.
Longer than a resuscitation. Shorter than a shift.
Emergency drawers only — never the genetics drawer.
Generated by the system, not by somebody's decision.
Every clinician's lifetime count is visible.
Twice a year in real emergencies is invisible.
Eleven times a month is not.
Split the record into about twenty separately locked drawers. Split each drawer into
individually sealed envelopes. Hand out only the keys a person actually needs.
…and five more. Restricted drawers in violet.
A key cuts the keys below it.
From a leaf you cannot reach its
parent; from one branch you cannot
Every participating organisation holds a copy.
Entries can be added, never altered.
No medical data in the log — only who looked at what,
and every refusal alongside every look.
Whose records were exposed, and which parts?
A query — not a three-week investigation.
48 hours in Kenya. 72 hours under GDPR.
Not a promise about the screen —
…and only for patients they are treating.
Excluded by arithmetic, not by contract.
CHOSEN FOR THE LENGTH OF A LIFE, NOT A PROCUREMENT CYCLE
ML-KEM-1024 + X448 · ML-DSA-87 + Ed448 · AES-256-GCM with key commitment · hash-only notarisation of history
